Rapper Macklemore dropped from Ed Sheeran's US tour after pro-Palestinian remarks

American rapper Macklemore announced Monday that he was dropped from British singer Ed Sheeran’s US stadium tour after saying "Free Palestine" during a September 4 concert in New Jersey. The Grammy winner’s removal follows pressure from venue owners, including New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft, over his criticism of Israel’s actions in Gaza.

corpus.title: Pro-Israel billionaire Robert Kraft led campaign to drop Macklemore from Ed Sheeran tour
corpus.signal_text:
Pro-Israel billionaire Robert Kraft led campaign to drop Macklemore from Ed Sheeran tour
In a statement shared on Instagram, US rapper Macklemore confirmed that “Ed Sheeran and his team” had dropped him from the tour after he said “Free Palestine”.
The campaign to remove Macklemore from the tour was driven by billionaire Robert Kraft, owner of the New England Patriots and Gillette Stadium, who threatened to block Sheeran and his team from using his stadium.
Kraft also rallied other stadium owners across the country to stop the tour from proceeding.
“Ed told me that Kraft said I would not be allowed to perform in his stadium,” Macklemore wrote.
“Ed also told me that Kraft had rallied some of the other stadium owners and collectively they gave him an ultimatum: 'If Macklemore stays on the tour, you will not be allowed to play in our venues.'”

According to Macklemore, Sheeran told him that he “doesn’t take sides” on Israel’s genocide in Gaza or its occupation of the Palestinian territories.
Kraft, who is a Jewish-American and passionate advocate of Israel, once led a group of hall of famer American footballers on a tour of Israel, in which he met Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Speaking in Israel in 2019, Kraft told the audience: “After my family, there is nothing I’m more passionate about than the State of Israel and my Jewish identity.”
In 2024, Kraft also withdrew his support from Columbia University after pro-Palestinian demonstrations against Israel's genocide were allowed to happen, saying it was “no longer an institution I recognise".
'The victims are the Palestinian people'
The campaign to silence Macklemore followed his appearances at Ed Sheeran’s MetLife Stadium shows in New Jersey last week, where he told the crowds that he wanted the people of Gaza and the West Bank to know that their plight at the hands of Israel had not been forgotten.
Macklemore, 43, whose real name is Benjamin Haggerty, then told the crowd “Free Palestine” and condemned Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza and apartheid in the occupied West Bank.
He was received with cheers from large sections of the crowd but indirectly subjected Sheeran, known for his play-by-the-book apolitical persona, to attacks by the pro-Israel right.
